sentences.es: Matt llega a la Ciudad de México en la noche.
sentences.en: Matt arrives in Mexico City at night.
sentences.gist: He lands in Mexico City late.

words.en: at night (Mexico; Spain says 'por la noche')

sentences.es: El aeropuerto es muy grande y hay mucha gente.
sentences.en: The airport is very big and there are a lot of people.

sentences.es: Primero, Matt pasa por migración y enseña su pasaporte.
sentences.en: First, Matt goes through immigration and shows his passport.

sentences.es: —¿Viene de vacaciones? —pregunta la agente.
sentences.en: "Are you here on vacation?" the officer asks.
sentences.gist: The officer asks why he's visiting.

sentences.es: —Sí, de vacaciones —contesta Matt.
sentences.en: "Yes, on vacation," Matt answers.

sentences.es: Después, Matt busca su maleta.
sentences.en: Afterwards, Matt looks for his suitcase.
sentences.gist: Now he has to find his bag.

sentences.es: La maleta tarda mucho, pero por fin llega.
sentences.en: The suitcase takes a long time, but it finally arrives.
sentences.gist: Long wait, but the bag shows up.

sentences.es: Luego, Matt cambia dinero y compra un chip para su celular.
sentences.en: Then Matt changes some money and buys a SIM card for his phone.
sentences.gist: He gets pesos and a Mexican SIM.
sentences.natural: Luego, Matt cambia dinero y compra un chip pa' su celular.

sentences.es: Está cansado, pero está muy contento.
sentences.en: He's tired, but he's very happy.
sentences.gist: Tired but glad to be there.
sentences.natural: 'Tá cansado, pero 'tá muy contento.

sentences.es: Matt necesita ir a su hotel en la colonia Roma.
sentences.en: Matt needs to go to his hotel in the Roma neighborhood.
sentences.gist: He has to get to his hotel.

sentences.es: Pide un Uber con su celular.
sentences.en: He orders an Uber on his phone.
sentences.gist: He calls a ride with an app.

sentences.es: En cinco minutos llega un carro blanco.
sentences.en: In five minutes a white car arrives.

sentences.es: —¿Matt? —pregunta el chofer. —Sí, soy yo.
sentences.en: "Matt?" the driver asks. "Yes, that's me."
sentences.gist: The driver checks it's the right passenger.

sentences.es: El chofer se llama Javier y es muy amable.
sentences.en: The driver's name is Javier and he's very friendly.

sentences.es: Hay mucho tráfico, como siempre.
sentences.en: There's a lot of traffic, as always.
sentences.gist: Traffic is bad — that's normal here.

sentences.es: Javier pone música y platica con Matt de fútbol.
sentences.en: Javier puts on some music and chats with Matt about soccer.

sentences.es: Después de cuarenta minutos, llegan al hotel.
sentences.en: After forty minutes, they arrive at the hotel.
sentences.gist: It's a long ride, but they make it.

words.en: arrive at the (llegar; al = a + el)

sentences.es: Matt paga con la app y le da las gracias a Javier.
sentences.en: Matt pays through the app and thanks Javier.
sentences.gist: He pays and says thank you.

sentences.es: Son las diez de la noche y Matt tiene hambre.
sentences.en: It's ten at night and Matt is hungry.

sentences.es: En la esquina hay una taquería con mucha gente.
sentences.en: On the corner there's a taquería with lots of people.
sentences.gist: A busy taco place is close by.

sentences.es: El taquero corta la carne al pastor del trompo.
sentences.en: The taquero cuts the al pastor meat off the spit.
sentences.gist: The cook slices the pork for the tacos.

sentences.es: —¿Qué le damos, joven? —pregunta el taquero.
sentences.en: "What can we get you, young man?" the taquero asks.

words.en: what can we get you? (lit. what do we give you)
young man (polite way to address a man)

sentences.es: —Cuatro de pastor con todo, por favor.
sentences.en: "Four al pastor with everything, please."
sentences.gist: He orders four tacos, fully loaded.
sentences.natural: Cuatro de pastor con to'o, porfa.

sentences.es: Matt le pone salsa verde y un poco de limón.
sentences.en: Matt adds green salsa and a little lime.

sentences.es: La salsa pica mucho, pero los tacos están deliciosos.
sentences.en: The salsa is really spicy, but the tacos are delicious.

sentences.es: También toma un agua de horchata bien fría.
sentences.en: He also has a nice cold horchata.
sentences.gist: He gets a cold drink too.

sentences.es: —¿Cuánto le debo? —Son ochenta pesos, joven.
sentences.en: "How much do I owe you?" "That's eighty pesos, young man."

words.en: how much do I owe you? (deber)

sentences.es: Hay un OXXO en casi todas las esquinas de México.
sentences.en: There's an OXXO on almost every corner in Mexico.

sentences.es: Matt entra porque tiene sed.
sentences.en: Matt goes in because he's thirsty.

sentences.es: Abre el refri y saca una botella de agua.
sentences.en: He opens the fridge and takes out a bottle of water.
sentences.gist: He grabs water from the cooler.

sentences.es: También agarra unas papitas y un pan dulce.
sentences.en: He also grabs some chips and a sweet roll.

sentences.es: En la caja, la cajera pregunta: —¿Es todo?
sentences.en: At the register, the cashier asks: "Is that everything?"
sentences.gist: At checkout she asks if he's done.
sentences.natural: En la caja, la cajera pregunta: ¿Es to'o?

sentences.es: —Sí, es todo. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
sentences.en: "Yes, that's all. Can I pay by card?"
sentences.gist: He asks to pay with his card.
sentences.natural: Sí, es to'o. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?

sentences.es: —Claro. Son sesenta y cinco pesos.
sentences.en: "Sure. That's sixty-five pesos."

sentences.es: Luego la cajera pregunta: —¿Gusta redondear?
sentences.en: Then the cashier asks: "Would you like to round up?"
sentences.gist: She offers to round up the total and donate the change.

words.en: to round up (the extra goes to charity)

sentences.es: Matt no entiende, pero dice que sí y sonríe.
sentences.en: Matt doesn't understand, but he says yes and smiles.
sentences.gist: He agrees without knowing what it is.

sentences.es: Matt entra al hotel con su maleta.
sentences.en: Matt walks into the hotel with his suitcase.

words.en: goes into the (entrar; al = a + el)

sentences.es: —Buenas noches. Tengo una reservación a nombre de Matt.
sentences.en: "Good evening. I have a reservation under the name Matt."
sentences.gist: He says he has a booking.

sentences.es: La recepcionista busca en la computadora.
sentences.en: The receptionist looks on the computer.

sentences.es: —Sí, aquí está. Son tres noches, ¿verdad?
sentences.en: "Yes, here it is. It's three nights, right?"
sentences.gist: She finds it and confirms the dates.
sentences.natural: Sí, aquí 'tá. Son tres noches, ¿verdá?

sentences.es: —¿Me permite su pasaporte y una tarjeta, por favor?
sentences.en: "May I have your passport and a card, please?"
sentences.gist: She asks for ID and a card.

words.en: may I have / may I see…? (permitir; very polite)

sentences.es: Después, le da una llave y la contraseña del wifi.
sentences.en: Then she gives him a key and the wifi password.
sentences.gist: He gets his key and the wifi.

sentences.es: —Su cuarto está en el cuarto piso.
sentences.en: "Your room is on the fourth floor."
sentences.gist: Fun fact: 'cuarto' means both room and fourth.

sentences.es: —El desayuno es de siete a diez, en el restaurante.
sentences.en: "Breakfast is from seven to ten, in the restaurant."

sentences.es: Matt sube al cuarto, abre la ventana y escucha la ciudad.
sentences.en: Matt goes up to the room, opens the window and listens to the city.
sentences.gist: He settles in and takes in the city.

sentences.es: Es domingo y Matt sale temprano a caminar.
sentences.en: It's Sunday and Matt goes out early for a walk.

sentences.es: En la calle hay un café pequeño con mesas afuera.
sentences.en: On the street there's a small café with tables outside.

sentences.es: Matt se sienta y pide un café de olla.
sentences.en: Matt sits down and orders a café de olla.

sentences.es: El café de olla lleva canela y piloncillo.
sentences.en: Café de olla has cinnamon and piloncillo in it.

sentences.es: También pide un pan dulce: una concha de chocolate.
sentences.en: He also orders a pastry: a chocolate concha.
sentences.gist: He gets a sweet roll too.

sentences.es: La mesera es muy simpática y le pregunta si es su primera vez en México.
sentences.en: The waitress is very nice and asks him if it's his first time in Mexico.
sentences.gist: A friendly waitress makes small talk.

sentences.es: —Sí, es mi primera vez. ¡Todo es nuevo para mí!
sentences.en: "Yes, it's my first time. Everything is new to me!"
sentences.gist: He's new here and loving it.
sentences.natural: Sí, es mi primera vez. ¡To'o es nuevo pa' mí!

sentences.es: Matt lee las noticias en su celular y toma su café despacio.
sentences.en: Matt reads the news on his phone and drinks his coffee slowly.

sentences.es: Cuando termina, deja una propina del diez por ciento.
sentences.en: When he finishes, he leaves a ten percent tip.

sentences.es: Matt está en el Centro Histórico y busca el Zócalo.
sentences.en: Matt is in the historic downtown and he's looking for the Zócalo.
sentences.gist: He's trying to find the main square.

sentences.es: Tiene un mapa en el celular, pero no tiene batería.
sentences.en: He has a map on his phone, but the battery is dead.

sentences.es: Entonces le pregunta a una señora: —Disculpe, ¿dónde está el Zócalo?
sentences.en: So he asks a lady: "Excuse me, where's the Zócalo?"
sentences.gist: He asks someone on the street.
sentences.natural: Entonces le pregunta a una señora: Disculpe, ¿dónde 'tá el Zócalo?

sentences.es: —Está muy cerca, joven. Se va derecho por la calle Madero.
sentences.en: "It's very close, young man. You go straight down Madero Street."
sentences.natural: 'Tá muy cerca, joven. Se va derecho por la calle Madero.

sentences.es: —¿Derecho? ¿No doy vuelta a la izquierda?
sentences.en: "Straight? I don't turn left?"

sentences.es: —No, no. Todo derecho, unas cinco cuadras.
sentences.en: "No, no. Straight ahead, about five blocks."
sentences.natural: No, no. To'o derecho, unas cinco cuadras.

sentences.es: —Al final, a su izquierda, está la catedral.
sentences.en: "At the end, on your left, is the cathedral."
sentences.gist: The cathedral is the landmark to look for.

sentences.es: Matt le da las gracias y camina por Madero.
sentences.en: Matt thanks her and walks down Madero.

sentences.es: Diez minutos después, ve una bandera enorme: ¡es el Zócalo!
sentences.en: Ten minutes later he sees a huge flag: it's the Zócalo!

sentences.es: Suena el celular de Matt.
sentences.en: Matt's phone rings.

sentences.es: Es un número de México que no conoce.
sentences.en: It's a Mexican number he doesn't recognize.
sentences.gist: He doesn't know who it is.

sentences.es: Matt contesta: —¿Bueno?
sentences.en: Matt answers: "Hello?"
sentences.gist: In Mexico you answer the phone with '¿Bueno?'.

sentences.es: —Hola, ¿hablo con Matt? Soy Lupita, la amiga de Diego.
sentences.en: "Hi, is this Matt? I'm Lupita, Diego's friend."
sentences.gist: A friend of a friend is calling.

words.en: am I speaking with…?, is this…?

sentences.es: —¡Ah, hola, Lupita! ¿Qué tal?
sentences.en: "Oh, hi, Lupita! How's it going?"

sentences.es: —Bien, gracias. Oye, ¿estás libre el sábado?
sentences.en: "Good, thanks. Hey, are you free on Saturday?"
sentences.natural: Bien, gracias. Oye, ¿'tás libre el sábado?

sentences.es: —Mi familia hace una cena en la casa. ¿Quieres venir?
sentences.en: "My family is having a dinner at home. Do you want to come?"
sentences.gist: She invites him to a family dinner.

words.en: do you want to come? (querer, venir)

sentences.es: —¡Claro que sí! ¿A qué hora?
sentences.en: "Of course! What time?"

sentences.es: —A las ocho. Te mando la dirección por WhatsApp.
sentences.en: "At eight. I'll send you the address on WhatsApp."

words.en: I'll send you (mandar; present used for the near future)

sentences.es: Matt y Lupita van a hacer un viaje de un día.
sentences.en: Matt and Lupita are going to take a day trip.
sentences.gist: They're planning a day out of the city.

words.en: are going to do/take (ir a + infinitive)

sentences.es: —¿Adónde vamos? —pregunta Matt.
sentences.en: "Where are we going?" Matt asks.

sentences.es: —Vamos a ir a Puebla. Está a dos horas en camión.
sentences.en: "We're going to go to Puebla. It's two hours away by bus."
sentences.gist: Puebla, a short bus ride away.
sentences.natural: Vamos a ir a Puebla. 'Tá a dos horas en camión.

sentences.es: —Me gusta la idea. ¿Qué hay en Puebla?
sentences.en: "I like that idea. What is there in Puebla?"

sentences.es: —Hay iglesias muy bonitas, talavera y, sobre todo, mucha comida rica.
sentences.en: "There are beautiful churches, talavera pottery and, above all, lots of delicious food."
sentences.gist: Puebla is famous for churches, ceramics and food.
sentences.natural: Hay iglesias muy bonitas, talavera y, sobre to'o, mucha comida rica.

sentences.es: —¡Tienes que probar el mole poblano!
sentences.en: "You have to try mole poblano!"

sentences.es: Deciden salir temprano, a las siete de la mañana.
sentences.en: They decide to leave early, at seven in the morning.

sentences.es: —Entonces me voy a levantar a las cinco y media —dice Matt.
sentences.en: "Then I'm going to get up at five thirty," Matt says.
sentences.gist: He'll have to wake up very early.
sentences.natural: Entonces me voya levantar a las cinco y media.

sentences.es: —Sí, y vamos a comprar los boletos en línea esta noche.
sentences.en: "Yes, and we're going to buy the tickets online tonight."

sentences.es: —El camión sale de la TAPO, la terminal de oriente.
sentences.en: "The bus leaves from TAPO, the eastern bus station."

sentences.es: Matt está muy emocionado: le encanta conocer lugares nuevos.
sentences.en: Matt is really excited: he loves seeing new places.

words.en: to get to know, to visit (a place)

sentences.es: Son las ocho de la mañana y Matt quiere ir al Museo de Antropología.
sentences.en: It's eight in the morning and Matt wants to go to the Anthropology Museum.
sentences.gist: He has a museum to get to.

sentences.es: Puede tomar un Uber, pero hay mucho tráfico, así que decide tomar el metro.
sentences.en: He could take an Uber, but there's a lot of traffic, so he decides to take the metro.

sentences.es: En la taquilla, compra una tarjeta y le recarga cien pesos.
sentences.en: At the ticket window, he buys a card and tops it up with a hundred pesos.

sentences.es: Cada viaje cuesta solo cinco pesos.
sentences.en: Each ride costs only five pesos.

sentences.es: Pero a esta hora, el andén está lleno de gente.
sentences.en: But at this hour, the platform is packed with people.

sentences.es: Llega el tren y todos empujan para subir.
sentences.en: The train arrives and everyone pushes to get on.

sentences.es: Un señor le explica a Matt: —A esta hora, los primeros vagones son solo para mujeres y niños.
sentences.en: A man explains to Matt: "At this time of day, the first cars are only for women and children."
sentences.gist: The front cars are reserved at rush hour.

sentences.es: Matt camina hacia la parte de atrás del andén y espera el siguiente tren.
sentences.en: Matt walks toward the back of the platform and waits for the next train.

sentences.es: Adentro, un vendedor grita: —¡Chicles, chicles, a diez pesos!
sentences.en: Inside, a vendor shouts: "Gum, gum, ten pesos!"
sentences.gist: Vendors sell things on the train.

sentences.es: Matt tiene que cambiar de línea una vez.
sentences.en: Matt has to change lines once.

sentences.es: Cuando por fin sale a la calle, piensa: “¡Puedo sobrevivir al metro de la Ciudad de México!”
sentences.en: When he finally comes out onto the street, he thinks: "I can survive the Mexico City metro!"
sentences.gist: He made it, and he's proud.

sentences.es: Los domingos, Matt y Lupita van al mercado de Coyoacán.
sentences.en: On Sundays, Matt and Lupita go to the Coyoacán market.

sentences.es: El mercado huele a fruta, a flores y a comida.
sentences.en: The market smells of fruit, flowers and food.

words.en: smells of, smells like (oler — irregular: huele)

sentences.es: Primero se sientan a comer tostadas, porque el mercado es famoso por ellas.
sentences.en: First they sit down to eat tostadas, because the market is famous for them.
sentences.gist: They start with the market's famous dish.

sentences.es: —Yo quiero una de tinga y una de camarón —dice Lupita.
sentences.en: "I want one tinga and one shrimp," says Lupita.

sentences.es: —¿La salsa pica? —pregunta Matt.
sentences.en: "Is the salsa spicy?" Matt asks.

sentences.es: —No, joven, no pica nada —dice la señora.
sentences.en: "No, young man, it's not spicy at all," says the lady.

sentences.es: Matt prueba la salsa y empieza a llorar.
sentences.en: Matt tries the salsa and starts to cry.

sentences.es: Lupita se ríe: —En México, “no pica” significa “pica un poquito”.
sentences.en: Lupita laughs: "In Mexico, 'it's not spicy' means 'it's a little spicy.'"

sentences.es: Después, caminan por los puestos de artesanías.
sentences.en: Afterwards, they walk through the handicraft stalls.

sentences.es: Matt encuentra un alebrije de muchos colores y pregunta el precio.
sentences.en: Matt finds a very colorful alebrije and asks the price.

sentences.es: —Cuesta cuatrocientos, pero se lo dejo en trescientos cincuenta.
sentences.en: "It's four hundred, but I'll let you have it for three hundred fifty."
sentences.gist: The seller offers a small discount.

words.en: I'll let you have it for (dejar; bargaining phrase)

sentences.es: Los viernes hay lucha libre en la Arena México.
sentences.en: On Fridays there's lucha libre at Arena México.

sentences.es: Matt va con Diego y sus primos.
sentences.en: Matt goes with Diego and his cousins.

sentences.es: Afuera de la arena venden máscaras de todos los colores.
sentences.en: Outside the arena they sell masks in every color.

sentences.es: —Yo conozco a todos los luchadores —dice Diego, muy orgulloso.
sentences.en: "I know all the wrestlers," says Diego, very proud.

sentences.es: Matt compra una máscara azul y se la pone.
sentences.en: Matt buys a blue mask and puts it on.

sentences.es: Diego le explica: —Los técnicos son los buenos y los rudos son los malos.
sentences.en: Diego explains to him: "The técnicos are the good guys and the rudos are the bad guys."

sentences.es: —Yo siempre le voy a los rudos —dice un primo.
sentences.en: "I always root for the rudos," says one of the cousins.

words.en: I root for, I support (irle a, Mexico)

sentences.natural: Yo siempre le voya los rudos.

sentences.es: La gente grita, silba y aplaude.
sentences.en: The crowd shouts, whistles and claps.

words.en: the people, the crowd (takes a singular verb)

sentences.es: Un luchador salta desde las cuerdas y cae sobre otro.
sentences.en: A wrestler jumps off the ropes and lands on another one.

sentences.es: Matt no sabe las reglas, pero grita como todos.
sentences.en: Matt doesn't know the rules, but he shouts like everyone else.
sentences.gist: He doesn't get it, but he loves it.

sentences.es: Al final, Matt dice: —El próximo viernes, yo traigo a mis amigos.
sentences.en: At the end, Matt says: "Next Friday, I'm bringing my friends."

sentences.es: Matt se despierta con dolor de estómago.
sentences.en: Matt wakes up with a stomachache.

sentences.es: Cree que es por los tacos de la calle.
sentences.en: He thinks it's because of the street tacos.

sentences.es: Va a la farmacia de la esquina.
sentences.en: He goes to the pharmacy on the corner.

sentences.es: —Buenos días. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar? —pregunta el farmacéutico.
sentences.en: "Good morning. How can I help you?" asks the pharmacist.

words.en: how can I help you? (poder, ayudar)

sentences.es: —Me duele mucho el estómago y tengo un poco de fiebre.
sentences.en: "My stomach hurts a lot and I have a bit of a fever."

words.en: it hurts me (doler; works like gustar)

sentences.es: —¿Le duele también la cabeza?
sentences.en: "Does your head hurt too?"

sentences.es: —No, la cabeza no. Solo el estómago.
sentences.en: "No, not my head. Just my stomach."

sentences.es: —Le recomiendo este suero y estas pastillas.
sentences.en: "I recommend this electrolyte drink and these pills."
sentences.gist: He gets a rehydration drink and some pills.

sentences.es: —Se toma una pastilla cada ocho horas, con comida.
sentences.en: "You take one pill every eight hours, with food."

sentences.es: —Y si no se siente mejor en dos días, tiene que ir al médico.
sentences.en: "And if you don't feel better in two days, you need to see a doctor."
sentences.gist: See a doctor if it doesn't improve.

sentences.es: Junto a muchas farmacias hay un consultorio, y la consulta cuesta muy poco.
sentences.en: Next to many pharmacies there's a doctor's office, and a visit costs very little.
sentences.gist: In Mexico a cheap doctor is often right next to the pharmacy.

title: Cena con la familia de Lupita

sentences.es: El sábado en la noche, Matt va a cenar a casa de Lupita.
sentences.en: On Saturday night, Matt goes to Lupita's house for dinner.

sentences.es: Lleva flores para su mamá y un pastel de tres leches.
sentences.en: He brings flowers for her mom and a tres leches cake.

sentences.es: —¡Pásale, pásale! Estás en tu casa —dice la mamá de Lupita.
sentences.en: "Come in, come in! Make yourself at home," says Lupita's mom.

words.en: make yourself at home (lit. you're in your house)

sentences.natural: ¡Pásale, pásale! 'Tás en tu casa.

sentences.es: Lupita le presenta a toda su familia: sus papás, su hermano Toño y su abuela.
sentences.en: Lupita introduces him to her whole family: her parents, her brother Toño and her grandmother.

sentences.es: Su abuela tiene noventa años y todavía cocina todos los días.
sentences.en: Her grandmother is ninety and still cooks every day.
sentences.gist: Grandma is old but still the cook.

sentences.es: Hoy prepara pozole, la especialidad de la casa.
sentences.en: Today she's making pozole, the house specialty.

sentences.es: —¿Te gusta el pozole, mijo? —le pregunta la abuela.
sentences.en: "Do you like pozole, dear?" the grandmother asks him.
sentences.gist: Grandma wants to know if he likes it.

sentences.es: —¡Me encanta! Este pozole está buenísimo.
sentences.en: "I love it! This pozole is amazing."

sentences.es: Toño le pregunta a Matt si le gusta el fútbol y cuál es su equipo.
sentences.en: Toño asks Matt if he likes soccer and which team he supports.

sentences.es: —Mi equipo es el América —dice Toño—, pero mi papá le va a los Pumas.
sentences.en: "My team is América," says Toño, "but my dad roots for Pumas."
sentences.gist: Father and son support rival teams.

sentences.es: Todos se ríen, y la cena dura hasta la medianoche.
sentences.en: Everyone laughs, and dinner goes on until midnight.

title: La ofrenda
level_note: present + ir a + reflexive verbs, ~150 words

sentences.es: Es el 31 de octubre, y en casa de Lupita todos se preparan para el Día de Muertos.
sentences.en: It's October 31st, and at Lupita's house everyone is getting ready for the Day of the Dead.
sentences.gist: The family prepares for the holiday.

sentences.es: Van a poner una ofrenda en la sala para recordar al abuelo Chuy y a la tía Rosa.
sentences.en: They're going to set up an ofrenda in the living room to remember Grandpa Chuy and Aunt Rosa.
sentences.gist: The altar honors family members who have died.

words.en: are going to set up (ir a + poner)
altar of offerings for the dead

sentences.es: Primero ponen una mesa con tres niveles y la cubren con un mantel blanco.
sentences.en: First they set up a table with three levels and cover it with a white tablecloth.
sentences.gist: They build the base of the altar.

sentences.es: Lupita se encarga de las flores de cempasúchil.
sentences.en: Lupita is in charge of the cempasúchil flowers.

words.en: takes care of, is in charge of (encargarse)

sentences.es: —Su color y su olor guían a las almas hasta la casa —explica.
sentences.en: "Their color and their smell guide the souls to the house," she explains.
sentences.gist: The flowers show the dead the way home.

sentences.es: Toño pone las fotos del abuelo y de la tía, y unas velas.
sentences.en: Toño puts out the photos of Grandpa and of the aunt, and some candles.
sentences.gist: Photos and candles go on the altar.

sentences.es: La abuela pone pan de muerto, mole y una cerveza: la favorita del abuelo.
sentences.en: Grandma puts out pan de muerto, mole and a beer — Grandpa's favorite.
sentences.gist: They offer the food and drink the dead loved.

words.en: sweet bread made for Day of the Dead

sentences.es: También hay un vaso de agua, porque las almas llegan con sed después de un viaje largo.
sentences.en: There's also a glass of water, because the souls arrive thirsty after a long journey.
sentences.gist: Water is for the thirsty travellers from the other side.

sentences.es: Matt y Toño cuelgan papel picado de colores arriba de la ofrenda.
sentences.en: Matt and Toño hang colorful papel picado above the ofrenda.

sentences.es: Al final, la abuela prende el copal y se sienta frente a la ofrenda.
sentences.en: At the end, Grandma lights the copal and sits down in front of the ofrenda.

sentences.es: —Mañana y pasado mañana nos visitan nuestros muertos —dice, contenta.
sentences.en: "Tomorrow and the day after, our dead come to visit us," she says happily.
sentences.gist: November 1 and 2 are when the dead return — a happy time.

sentences.es: El martes, Matt salió solo a caminar por la colonia Condesa.
sentences.en: On Tuesday, Matt went out alone for a walk around the Condesa neighborhood.
sentences.gist: He went exploring on his own.

sentences.es: Caminó mucho y no miró el mapa ni una vez.
sentences.en: He walked a lot and didn't look at the map even once.
sentences.gist: He wandered without checking where he was.

sentences.es: De repente, se dio cuenta de que no sabía dónde estaba.
sentences.en: Suddenly, he realized he didn't know where he was.

sentences.es: Su celular no tenía señal, y además empezó a llover.
sentences.en: His phone had no signal, and on top of that it started to rain.

sentences.es: Se acercó a una señora que paseaba a su perro.
sentences.en: He went up to a lady who was walking her dog.
sentences.gist: He asked a stranger for help.

sentences.es: —Disculpe, ¿sabe dónde está la estación Chapultepec?
sentences.en: "Excuse me, do you know where Chapultepec station is?"

sentences.es: —¿Mande? —contestó la señora. Con la lluvia no escuchó bien.
sentences.en: "Sorry?" the lady answered. With the rain, she hadn't heard well.

sentences.es: Matt repitió la pregunta más despacio.
sentences.en: Matt repeated the question more slowly.

sentences.es: —Ah, pues está un poco lejos, joven. Este… ¿sabe qué? Yo voy para allá. Lo acompaño.
sentences.en: "Oh, well, it's a bit far, young man. Um… you know what? I'm going that way. I'll walk with you."
sentences.gist: She offers to walk him there.
sentences.natural: Ah, pos 'tá un poco lejos, joven. Este… ¿sabe qué? Yo voy pa'llá. Lo acompaño.

sentences.es: La señora abrió su paraguas y caminaron juntos diez cuadras.
sentences.en: The lady opened her umbrella and they walked ten blocks together.

sentences.es: En el camino, le preguntó de dónde era y le recomendó unos tacos buenísimos.
sentences.en: On the way, she asked him where he was from and recommended some amazing tacos.
sentences.gist: They chatted, and she gave him a food tip.

sentences.es: Cuando llegaron a la estación, Matt le dio las gracias mil veces.
sentences.en: When they got to the station, Matt thanked her a thousand times.

sentences.es: —No hay de qué, joven. ¡Para eso estamos!
sentences.en: "Don't mention it, young man. That's what we're here for!"
sentences.natural: No hay de qué, joven. ¡Pa' eso 'stamos!

sentences.es: Anoche Matt llegó al hotel muy cansado.
sentences.en: Last night Matt got back to the hotel very tired.

sentences.es: Se metió a bañar, pero no había agua caliente.
sentences.en: He got in the shower, but there was no hot water.

words.en: got in the shower (meterse a bañar, Mexico)

sentences.es: Además, la ventana no cerraba bien y el ruido de la calle no lo dejó dormir.
sentences.en: Also, the window didn't close properly and the street noise kept him awake.

sentences.es: En la mañana fue a la recepción.
sentences.en: In the morning he went to the front desk.

words.en: went (ir; same form as 'was' from ser)

sentences.es: —Buenos días. Este… tuve unos problemas con mi cuarto anoche.
sentences.en: "Good morning. Um… I had a few problems with my room last night."

sentences.es: —¿Mande? ¿Qué pasó, joven? —preguntó el recepcionista.
sentences.en: "Sorry? What happened, young man?" asked the receptionist.
sentences.gist: The receptionist asks what went wrong.

sentences.es: Matt le explicó todo: el agua fría, la ventana y el ruido.
sentences.en: Matt explained everything to him: the cold water, the window and the noise.

sentences.es: —Ay, discúlpenos. Es que ayer hubo un problema con el bóiler.
sentences.en: "Oh, we're so sorry. The thing is, there was a problem with the water heater yesterday."

sentences.es: —Ahorita le cambiamos de cuarto, ¿sí?
sentences.en: "We'll move you to another room right away, OK?"
sentences.gist: They promise a new room soon.

words.en: right now… or 'in a bit' (Mexico; it can stretch!)
we'll move you to another room (cambiar)

sentences.es: Matt esperó… y esperó. Ese “ahorita” duró casi una hora.
sentences.en: Matt waited… and waited. That "right away" lasted almost an hour.
sentences.gist: 'Ahorita' turned out to be a long time.

sentences.es: Por fin, el recepcionista vino con una llave nueva.
sentences.en: Finally, the receptionist came with a new key.

sentences.es: El cuarto nuevo estaba en el último piso, tenía vista a la ciudad y era muy tranquilo.
sentences.en: The new room was on the top floor, had a view of the city and was very quiet.
sentences.gist: The new room was much better.

sentences.es: —¡Órale! —dijo Matt—. Valió la pena esperar.
sentences.en: "Wow!" said Matt. "It was worth the wait."

words.en: it was worth it (valer la pena)

title: Un fin de semana en Oaxaca

sentences.es: El fin de semana pasado, Matt y Diego fueron a Oaxaca.
sentences.en: Last weekend, Matt and Diego went to Oaxaca.

sentences.es: Tomaron un camión de noche y llegaron a las seis de la mañana.
sentences.en: They took an overnight bus and arrived at six in the morning.

sentences.es: Hacía frío, pero el amanecer estaba precioso.
sentences.en: It was cold, but the sunrise was gorgeous.

sentences.es: Primero desayunaron chocolate caliente con pan de yema en un mercado.
sentences.en: First they had hot chocolate with egg-yolk bread for breakfast at a market.

sentences.es: Después fueron a Monte Albán, una antigua ciudad zapoteca.
sentences.en: Then they went to Monte Albán, an ancient Zapotec city.

sentences.es: —Esta ciudad tiene más de dos mil años —les dijo el guía.
sentences.en: "This city is more than two thousand years old," the guide told them.

words.es: tiene más de dos mil años
words.en: is more than two thousand years old

sentences.es: En la tarde, Diego le dijo a Matt: —Tienes que probar los chapulines.
sentences.en: In the afternoon, Diego told Matt: "You have to try the chapulines."
sentences.gist: Diego dares him to try a local snack.

sentences.es: —¿Chapulines? ¿Insectos? ¡No manches! —contestó Matt.
sentences.en: "Chapulines? Insects? No way!" Matt answered.

sentences.es: Pero los probó y, la verdad, estaban muy buenos: crujientes, con limón y chile.
sentences.en: But he tried them, and honestly, they were really good: crunchy, with lime and chile.
sentences.gist: He tried them and liked them.

sentences.es: En la noche cenaron una tlayuda enorme y tomaron un mezcal.
sentences.en: At night they had a huge tlayuda for dinner and drank a mezcal.

sentences.es: —Pues, ¿qué te pareció Oaxaca? —le preguntó Diego en el camión de regreso.
sentences.en: "So, what did you think of Oaxaca?" Diego asked him on the bus back.
sentences.gist: Diego asks how he liked it.

words.en: what did you think of it? (parecer)

sentences.natural: Pos, ¿qué te pareció Oaxaca? le preguntó Diego en el camión de regreso.

sentences.es: —Fue el mejor fin de semana del viaje. ¡Quiero volver!
sentences.en: "It was the best weekend of the trip. I want to go back!"

sentences.es: El domingo, Matt fue al estadio de Ciudad Universitaria con Toño y su papá, don Beto.
sentences.en: On Sunday, Matt went to the stadium at Ciudad Universitaria with Toño and his dad, don Beto.

words.en: respectful title used with a first name

sentences.es: Jugaban los Pumas contra el América: el clásico capitalino.
sentences.en: Pumas were playing América: the Mexico City derby.

sentences.es: Don Beto llevaba su playera de los Pumas, y Toño llevaba la del América.
sentences.en: Don Beto was wearing his Pumas jersey, and Toño was wearing his América one.
sentences.gist: Father and son wore rival shirts.

sentences.es: El estadio estaba lleno y la gente cantaba sin parar.
sentences.en: The stadium was full and people were singing nonstop.

sentences.es: Hacía sol, y vendían refrescos, cacahuates y papas con chile y limón.
sentences.en: It was sunny, and they were selling sodas, peanuts and chips with chile and lime.

sentences.es: En el minuto veinte, el América metió un gol.
sentences.en: In the twentieth minute, América scored a goal.

sentences.es: —¡Goooool! —gritó Toño, y su papá lo miró muy serio.
sentences.en: "Goooal!" shouted Toño, and his dad gave him a very serious look.

sentences.es: —Ahorita empatamos, ya vas a ver —dijo don Beto.
sentences.en: "We'll tie it up any minute now, you'll see," said don Beto.
sentences.gist: Dad is sure Pumas will equalize.
sentences.natural: Ahorita empatamos, ya vasa ver, dijo don Beto.

sentences.es: Durante el segundo tiempo, los Pumas atacaban y atacaban, pero no anotaban.
sentences.en: During the second half, Pumas kept attacking and attacking, but they weren't scoring.

sentences.es: Por fin, en el minuto noventa, un delantero de los Pumas anotó de cabeza.
sentences.en: Finally, in the ninetieth minute, a Pumas striker scored with a header.

sentences.es: Don Beto saltó, abrazó a Matt y gritó: —¡Órale! ¡Te lo dije!
sentences.en: Don Beto jumped up, hugged Matt and shouted: "Yes! I told you!"

sentences.es: —¡No manches, qué partidazo! —dijo Matt.
sentences.en: "No way, what a game!" said Matt.

sentences.es: Al final quedaron uno a uno, y todos regresaron a casa contentos… bueno, más o menos.
sentences.en: In the end it finished one all, and everyone went home happy… well, more or less.

sentences.es: La noche del primero de noviembre, Matt fue al panteón con la familia de Lupita.
sentences.en: On the night of November 1st, Matt went to the cemetery with Lupita's family.
sentences.gist: A Day of the Dead night visit to the graves.

sentences.es: El panteón estaba en el pueblo de la abuela, a una hora de la ciudad.
sentences.en: The cemetery was in Grandma's hometown, an hour from the city.
sentences.gist: They drove out to Grandma's town.

sentences.es: Cuando llegaron, ya había mucha gente.
sentences.en: When they arrived, there were already a lot of people.

sentences.es: Las tumbas estaban cubiertas de cempasúchil, y miles de velas iluminaban la noche.
sentences.en: The graves were covered in marigolds, and thousands of candles lit up the night.

sentences.es: Unas familias comían tamales, otras cantaban, y unos señores tocaban la guitarra.
sentences.en: Some families were eating tamales, others were singing, and some men were playing the guitar.

sentences.es: Matt pensaba que iba a ser un lugar triste, pero no era así.
sentences.en: Matt had thought it would be a sad place, but it wasn't like that.

sentences.es: La familia limpió la tumba del abuelo y la decoró con flores.
sentences.en: The family cleaned Grandpa's grave and decorated it with flowers.

sentences.es: La abuela le contaba historias del abuelo mientras prendía las velas.
sentences.en: Grandma told him stories about Grandpa while she lit the candles.

sentences.es: —Tu abuelo era muy bromista, ¿verdad? —le preguntó Matt a Lupita.
sentences.en: "Your grandpa was a real joker, wasn't he?" Matt asked Lupita.
sentences.gist: Matt picks up on Grandpa's personality.

sentences.es: —Uy, sí. Siempre contaba chistes, hasta en los velorios —dijo Lupita, riéndose.
sentences.en: "Oh, yes. He was always telling jokes, even at wakes," said Lupita, laughing.
sentences.gist: He was funny even at funerals.

sentences.es: A las dos de la mañana hacía mucho frío.
sentences.en: At two in the morning it was very cold.

words.en: it was very cold (hacer, for weather)

sentences.es: Una señora de la tumba de al lado les ofreció: —¿Gustan un ponchecito?
sentences.en: A lady at the next grave offered them: "Would you like a little hot punch?"
sentences.gist: A neighbor shared a hot drink.

sentences.es: Esa noche, Matt entendió que el Día de Muertos no es para llorar, sino para recordar.
sentences.en: That night, Matt understood that the Day of the Dead isn't for crying, but for remembering.
sentences.gist: The holiday is about remembering, not mourning.

title: La historia del Día de Muertos
title_en: The history of the Day of the Dead
level_note: mixed tenses, short history piece, ~240 words

sentences.es: El Día de Muertos se celebra en México el 1 y el 2 de noviembre.
sentences.en: The Day of the Dead is celebrated in Mexico on November 1 and 2.

sentences.es: Sus raíces son muy antiguas: vienen de los pueblos indígenas, como los mexicas, también llamados aztecas.
sentences.en: Its roots are very old: they come from the Indigenous peoples, like the Mexica, also called the Aztecs.
sentences.gist: It started long before the Spanish arrived.

words.en: the Mexica (what the Aztecs called themselves)

sentences.es: Para los mexicas, la muerte no era el final, sino parte de un ciclo.
sentences.en: For the Mexica, death wasn't the end, but part of a cycle.
sentences.gist: Death was seen as part of life.

sentences.es: Creían que las almas viajaban al Mictlán, el mundo de los muertos, y que el viaje duraba cuatro años.
sentences.en: They believed that souls travelled to Mictlán, the world of the dead, and that the journey took four years.
sentences.gist: The dead made a long journey to the underworld.

sentences.es: Cada año celebraban fiestas para honrar a sus muertos con comida, flores y música.
sentences.en: Every year they held festivals to honor their dead with food, flowers and music.
sentences.gist: They honored the dead with celebrations.

sentences.es: Cuando llegaron los españoles en el siglo XVI, trajeron las fiestas católicas de Todos los Santos y de los Fieles Difuntos.
sentences.en: When the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, they brought the Catholic feasts of All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day.
sentences.gist: The Spanish brought their own days for the dead.

sentences.es: Las dos tradiciones se mezclaron, y por eso hoy hay cruces y veladoras junto a calaveras y cempasúchil.
sentences.en: The two traditions blended, and that's why today there are crosses and candles next to skulls and marigolds.
sentences.gist: Today's holiday is a mix of both.

sentences.es: Una de las imágenes más famosas de esta fiesta es la Catrina.
sentences.en: One of the most famous images of this holiday is La Catrina.

sentences.es: La creó el grabador José Guadalupe Posada a principios del siglo XX.
sentences.en: The engraver José Guadalupe Posada created it in the early 20th century.
sentences.gist: An artist named Posada drew her about a century ago.

sentences.es: Al principio se llamaba “La Calavera Garbancera” y se burlaba de los mexicanos que querían parecer europeos.
sentences.en: At first it was called "La Calavera Garbancera," and it made fun of Mexicans who wanted to look European.
sentences.gist: She started as a joke about people pretending to be something they weren't.

sentences.es: Años después, el pintor Diego Rivera le dio el nombre de “Catrina” y la pintó en un mural famoso.
sentences.en: Years later, the painter Diego Rivera gave her the name "Catrina" and painted her in a famous mural.
sentences.gist: Diego Rivera named her and made her famous.

sentences.es: Su mensaje sigue siendo el mismo: ricos o pobres, al final todos somos calaveras.
sentences.en: Her message is still the same: rich or poor, in the end we're all skeletons.

sentences.es: En 2008, la UNESCO reconoció esta tradición como Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Humanidad.
sentences.en: In 2008, UNESCO recognized this tradition as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

sentences.es: Desde 2016, la Ciudad de México también tiene un gran desfile, inspirado en una película de James Bond.
sentences.en: Since 2016, Mexico City has also had a big parade, inspired by a James Bond movie.
sentences.gist: The famous parade is actually new.

sentences.es: Cada región lo celebra a su manera, pero la idea es la misma: que nadie olvide a sus muertos.
sentences.en: Each region celebrates it in its own way, but the idea is the same: that no one forgets their dead.

title: La Llorona
level_note: mixed tenses, a legend retold simply, ~210 words

sentences.es: En México todos conocen la leyenda de La Llorona.
sentences.en: In Mexico everyone knows the legend of La Llorona.

sentences.es: Hay muchas versiones, pero esta es una de las más conocidas.
sentences.en: There are many versions, but this is one of the best known.

sentences.es: Hace muchos años, en un pueblo junto a un río, vivía una mujer llamada María.
sentences.en: Many years ago, in a village by a river, there lived a woman named María.
sentences.gist: The story starts with a woman by a river.

sentences.es: Era más hermosa que todas las mujeres del pueblo, y lo sabía.
sentences.en: She was more beautiful than all the women in the village, and she knew it.

sentences.es: Un día llegó un hombre rico, se enamoró de ella y se casaron.
sentences.en: One day a rich man arrived, fell in love with her, and they got married.

sentences.es: Tuvieron dos hijos, y al principio eran muy felices.
sentences.en: They had two children, and at first they were very happy.

sentences.es: Pero con el tiempo, el hombre salía cada vez más y ya no le hacía caso a María.
sentences.en: But over time, the man went out more and more and stopped paying attention to María.
sentences.gist: Her husband began to ignore her.

words.en: no longer paid attention to her (hacerle caso a)

sentences.es: Una tarde, María lo vio en el camino con otra mujer, más joven y más rica que ella.
sentences.en: One afternoon, María saw him on the road with another woman, younger and richer than she was.
sentences.gist: She caught him with someone else.

sentences.es: Loca de celos y de dolor, llevó a sus hijos al río y los ahogó.
sentences.en: Mad with jealousy and pain, she took her children to the river and drowned them.
sentences.gist: In her rage, she did something terrible.

sentences.es: Cuando entendió lo que había hecho, ya era demasiado tarde.
sentences.en: When she understood what she had done, it was already too late.
sentences.natural: Cuando entendió lo kabía hecho, ya era demasiado tarde.

sentences.es: María murió en la orilla del río, llorando por sus hijos.
sentences.en: María died on the riverbank, weeping for her children.

sentences.es: Desde entonces, su alma camina de noche cerca del agua, vestida de blanco.
sentences.en: Since then, her soul has walked at night near the water, dressed in white.

sentences.es: Dicen que grita “¡Ay, mis hijos!” y que nunca los va a encontrar.
sentences.en: They say she cries out "Oh, my children!" and that she will never find them.

sentences.es: Las abuelas les cuentan esta historia a los niños para que no salgan solos de noche.
sentences.en: Grandmothers tell this story to children so that they don't go out alone at night.
sentences.gist: It's a warning tale for kids.

words.en: so that they don't go out (salir, subjunctive)

sentences.es: Algunos historiadores dicen que la leyenda es aún más vieja que la Conquista: los mexicas ya hablaban de una mujer que lloraba de noche por sus hijos.
sentences.en: Some historians say the legend is even older than the Conquest: the Mexica already spoke of a woman who wept at night for her children.
sentences.gist: The legend may go back to Aztec times.

sentences.es: Esta mañana, poco después de las diez, sonó la alerta sísmica en la Ciudad de México.
sentences.en: This morning, shortly after ten, the earthquake alarm went off in Mexico City.
sentences.gist: The quake warning sounded this morning.

sentences.es: Casi un minuto después, la ciudad empezó a moverse.
sentences.en: Almost a minute later, the city started to shake.
sentences.gist: The shaking came a minute after the alarm.

sentences.es: Según el Servicio Sismológico Nacional, el sismo fue de magnitud 6.4 y su epicentro estaba en la costa de Guerrero.
sentences.en: According to the National Seismological Service, the quake was magnitude 6.4 and its epicenter was on the coast of Guerrero.
sentences.gist: A strong quake, centered far away on the coast.

sentences.es: Como el epicentro estaba lejos, la gente tuvo casi un minuto para reaccionar.
sentences.en: Because the epicenter was far away, people had almost a minute to react.

words.en: since, because (at the start of a sentence)

sentences.es: La alerta funciona así: unos sensores en la costa detectan el sismo y mandan una señal de radio a la ciudad.
sentences.en: The alert works like this: sensors on the coast detect the quake and send a radio signal to the city.

sentences.es: La señal viaja mucho más rápido que las ondas del sismo.
sentences.en: The signal travels much faster than the earthquake's waves.

sentences.es: Por eso, la alarma suele sonar antes de que se sienta el movimiento.
sentences.en: That's why the alarm usually goes off before the shaking is felt.
sentences.gist: You usually get a warning first.

sentences.es: El sistema funciona desde 1991, unos años después del terrible terremoto de 1985.
sentences.en: The system has been running since 1991, a few years after the terrible 1985 earthquake.
sentences.gist: It was built after a deadly quake.

words.en: has been working since (present tense + desde)

sentences.es: Miles de personas salieron de oficinas y escuelas, y esperaron en la calle con calma.
sentences.en: Thousands of people left offices and schools and waited calmly in the street.

sentences.es: En los altavoces se escuchaba la voz de siempre: “Alerta sísmica, alerta sísmica”.
sentences.en: On the loudspeakers you could hear the usual voice: "Earthquake alert, earthquake alert."
sentences.gist: The familiar warning played across the city.

sentences.es: —Acababa de entrar a una junta cuando sonó —contó Andrea, una oficinista de la colonia Juárez.
sentences.en: "I had just gone into a meeting when it went off," said Andrea, an office worker in the Juárez neighborhood.

words.en: had just gone in (acabar de + infinitive)

sentences.es: —Bajamos por las escaleras, como en los simulacros: no corro, no grito, no empujo.
sentences.en: "We went down the stairs, like in the drills: don't run, don't shout, don't push."
sentences.gist: They followed the official safety rule.

words.es: no corro, no grito, no empujo
words.en: the official motto: I don't run, shout or push

sentences.es: Hasta ahora, las autoridades no reportan daños graves ni personas heridas.
sentences.en: So far, the authorities are not reporting serious damage or injuries.

sentences.es: Protección Civil recuerda que no hay que usar los elevadores y que hay que alejarse de las ventanas.
sentences.en: Civil Protection reminds people not to use elevators and to stay away from windows.

sentences.es: Los capitalinos ya están acostumbrados, pero cada vez que suena la alerta, el corazón vuelve a latir rápido.
sentences.en: Mexico City residents are used to it by now, but every time the alert goes off, their hearts start racing again.
sentences.gist: People are used to it, but it still scares them.

title: Una carta de Lupita
level_note: mixed tenses, subjunctive in fixed phrases, ~170 words

sentences.es: Querido Matt: ¡Espero que estés muy bien!
sentences.en: Dear Matt: I hope you're doing really well!

sentences.es: Aquí en la casa todos te mandan saludos, sobre todo mi abuela.
sentences.en: Here at home everyone says hi, especially my grandma.

sentences.es: Desde que te fuiste, cada domingo pregunta: “¿Y Matt? ¿Estará comiendo bien?”
sentences.en: Since you left, every Sunday she asks: "And Matt? I wonder if he's eating well?"
sentences.gist: Grandma worries about him, like a true grandma.

words.en: I wonder if he's eating (future of probability)

sentences.es: Te cuento que Toño por fin consiguió trabajo en un banco.
sentences.en: Guess what: Toño finally got a job at a bank.

words.en: let me tell you, guess what (contar)

sentences.es: Ahora se levanta a las seis y se pone corbata todos los días. ¡No lo reconocerías!
sentences.en: Now he gets up at six and wears a tie every day. You wouldn't recognize him!

sentences.es: Mi papá todavía habla del gol de los Pumas en el minuto noventa.
sentences.en: My dad still talks about Pumas' goal in the ninetieth minute.

sentences.es: Yo me acordé mucho de ti cuando volví a Puebla el mes pasado.
sentences.en: I thought about you a lot when I went back to Puebla last month.

words.en: I thought about you a lot (acordarse de)

sentences.es: Comí mole en el mismo restaurante, y la mesera me preguntó por ti.
sentences.en: I had mole at the same restaurant, and the waitress asked me about you.

sentences.es: ¿Y tú? ¿Sigues practicando español?
sentences.en: And you? Are you still practicing Spanish?

sentences.es: Tu último mensaje de WhatsApp estaba casi perfecto. ¡Ya escribes como chilango!
sentences.en: Your last WhatsApp message was almost perfect. You write like a real chilango now!
sentences.gist: His Spanish has improved a lot.

sentences.es: Oye, el año que viene mi hermano se casa, y queremos que vengas a la boda.
sentences.en: Hey, next year my brother is getting married, and we want you to come to the wedding.

words.en: we want you to come (venir, subjunctive)

sentences.es: Va a ser en diciembre, en el pueblo de mi abuela.
sentences.en: It's going to be in December, in my grandma's hometown.

words.en: it's going to be (ir a + ser)

sentences.es: Ojalá que puedas venir; aquí siempre tienes casa.
sentences.en: I really hope you can come; you'll always have a home here.

words.en: you have a home, a place to stay

sentences.es: Bueno, te dejo porque ya me voy a trabajar.
sentences.en: Well, I'll let you go, because I'm heading off to work.

words.en: I'll let you go (dejar; common sign-off)

sentences.natural: Bueno, te dejo porque ya me voya trabajar.

sentences.es: Un abrazo muy fuerte, y que te vaya muy bien. Tu amiga, Lupita.
sentences.en: A big hug, and all the best. Your friend, Lupita.

words.en: all the best, take care (lit. may it go well for you; ir, subjunctive)
